Class MessageParamDateParser

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.MessageParamDateParser
public abstract class MessageParamDateParser extends Object
Reads a date or date-time out of the parameter map of a GTNetMessage.

The parameters travel between peers as plain strings, and the two producers do not agree on a format: the message dialog submits the raw value of a date form control, which serialises as an ISO instant with a trailing Z (2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z), while a peer driving the protocol directly sends what LocalDate.toString() produces (2026-09-01). A parser accepting only one of the two silently loses the value — closeStartDate used to be read with DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME, which throws on a bare date, so a discontinuation was never recognised as expired and its message never became deletable.

Both methods are lenient by design: an absent, blank or unparsable parameter yields null rather than an exception, because a malformed value from a remote peer must not abort the processing of the message.

    • isAnnouncementExpired

      public static boolean isAnnouncementExpired(GTNetMessage message)
      Whether a future-oriented announcement has run out: the maintenance window has ended, or the announced shutdown date has passed. The single answer for both callers that ask it — the delivery task before sending an announcement on, and the handshake handler before queuing one for a newly connected peer. They used to carry two copies that had drifted apart, and the closeStartDate branch of both rejected a plain yyyy-MM-dd.

      Anything that is not one of the two announcement codes, and any announcement whose date cannot be read, counts as not expired: dropping a message because its date is unreadable would hide it from the administrator.

      Parameters:
      message - the sent announcement to test
      Returns:
      true when the announcement no longer has any effect ahead of it
